instruction.text: Entscheide, ob die Aussagen richtig oder falsch sind.

atoms.a: Wenn du über einen Vorfall berichtest, solltest du alle 4 W-Fragen beantworten. Und zwar who, when, where und what.
Wenn du über einen Vorfall berichtest, solltest du Vermutungen wiedergeben.

wrong.text: Wenn du über einen Vorfall berichtest, solltest du keine Vermutungen, sondern immer nur Tatsachen wiedergeben.

atoms.a: Wenn du über einen Vorfall berichtest, solltest du die Geschehnisse in der richtigen Reihenfolge schildern.
Wenn du über einen Vorfall berichtest, musst du das will-future verwenden.

wrong.text: Wenn du über einen Vorfall berichtest, musst du das simple past verwenden.

atoms.a: Wenn du über einen Vorfall berichtest, solltest du viele Adjektive und Adverbien benutzen.

b: ++Mila dropped her water bottle and the water spilled everywhere. Ali wanted to help clean the floor, but he fell because it was slippery. Mila helped Ali up, and she asked if he was okay. Ali wasn't hurt, and they cleaned the floor together.

Ali wasn't hurt, and they cleaned the floor together. Mila helped Ali up, and she asked if he was okay. Ali wanted to help clean the floor, but he fell because it was slippery. Mila dropped her water bottle and the water spilled everywhere.

wrong.text: Achte darauf, dass die Ereignisse in der richtigen Reihenfolge erwähnt werden.

b: ++Ben couldn’t find his small, brown pencil case after art class. He looked carefully under the big table and asked his friends. Mia quickly found it near the white sink and gave it back. Ben gratefully said thank you and was extremely happy again.
Ben couldn’t find his pencil case after art class. He looked under the table and asked his friends. Mia found it near the sink and gave it back. Ben said thank you and was happy again.

wrong.text: Durch Adjektive und Adverbien wird der Bericht anschaulicher.

b: ++During break, Tim and Sarah bumped into each other while running. Tim fell down but wasn’t hurt. Sarah helped him up and said sorry. They kept playing together.
During break, Tim and Sarah bump into each other while running. Tim falls down but isn’t hurt. Sarah helps him up and says sorry. They keep playing together.

wrong.text: Achte auf die Zeitform! Berichte stehen im simple past.

b: ++Anna used her ruler in maths class. It suddenly fell down and broke. Paul saw it and gave her an extra ruler. Anna smiled and said thank you.
Anna used her ruler in maths class. I think it fell down and broke. I belive Paul saw it and gave her an extra ruler. I hope Anna smiled and said thank you.

wrong.text: In einem Bericht sollten nur Tatsachen erwähnt werden, keine Vermutungen.
